snapshot_markdown:
**Blue Energy Limited (ASX: BLU)** — Energy Exploration (Oil & Gas E&P, transitioning to gas-fired data center power and Small Modular Reactor development). Brisbane, Queensland, AU. 2 employees. Projects: Bowen Basin, Carpentaria Basin, Galilee Basin (CSG/conventional gas exploration); HyReward Project (strategic partnership); Sapphire 5L2 gas project; SMR development for data center applications.

## Situational read
This is a strategic vehicle, not a junior explorer. Two employees on paper, but $230.46M raised across 10 rounds since the 1994 IPO, and a cap table that reads like the Australian energy transition itself: **Stanwell** (Queensland state-owned generator) since 2008, **Korean Gas** since 2009, **IFM Investors** (Australia's largest pension manager) since 2018, plus **KKR**, **Green Investment Group**, and **Temporis Capital** on a $124.77M debt tranche from Dec 2015. Chairman is **John Ellice-Flint**, former Santos CEO. CEO/MD John Phillips runs operations solo.

The story is a deliberate pivot. From 2007 through ~2022, BLU was a Queensland CSG explorer drilling the Bowen and Carpentaria basins. Stock has lost 96% over 15 years on that thesis — gas markets and CSG economics didn't deliver. From 2023 onward, the company has been repositioning around **data center power infrastructure**: gas-fired generation as bridge, SMRs as the long-term play. Bloomberg confirms a **$380M raise in April 2026 to build nukes for data centers**. October 2024 raised $45M from Axios-reported investors for "underwater SMR" development. The HyReward Project from 2023 connects this to hydrogen co-generation.

This is exactly the kind of company that has institutional pressure to deliver, board-level operational pedigree, and zero functional operating team to execute. The $380M April raise puts a clock on it.

## Capital structure
**$230.46M raised across 10 disclosed rounds since 1994 IPO.** Mostly equity via PIPEs to strategic and institutional investors. Notable rounds: Aug 2008 PIPE ($31.6M), Jan 2007 PIPE ($34.7M), May 2009 PIPE ($7.17M), Jul 2022 PIPE ($13.68M), and most recently a small Aug 2025 PIPE ($3.2M). The headline-grabbing $380M April 2026 raise (per Bloomberg) is not yet in PitchBook's deal log but is consistent with the data center / SMR pivot.

**Dec 2015 Debt - General: $124.77M from Green Investment Group (UK), KKR, and Temporis Capital.** Active equity investors include IFM, Stanwell (QLD state generator), Korean Gas (KOGAS), Chimaera Capital, Mathews Capital, and Cornerstone Investments.

## Recent activity (last 6 months)
**The data center / SMR pivot is the dominant theme.** Apr 21, 2026 Bloomberg: $380M raise for data center nukes. Oct 30, 2025: Bloomberg + company release both flag the gas-then-nuclear data center plant plan. Sep 23, 2025: "Infra Dig" podcast appearance positioning BLU in the US nuclear scene. Earlier: Oct 2024 Axios scoop on $45M for underwater reactors. Sep 2023: HyReward strategic partnership (hydrogen). Sep 2023: Sapphire gas project updates (the legacy CSG asset).

## Top contacts for outreach
**Primary target:** **John Phillips** (CEO/MD, john.phillips@blueenergy.com.au, +61 7 3270 8800). He is the entire operating team. Pitch: you've got $380M of institutional capital, two employees, and a thesis that requires building gas-fired generation and ultimately commercial SMRs in Australia. That's the gap.

**Board-level escalation if Phillips doesn't engage:** **John Ellice-Flint** (Chairman, former Santos CEO). Frame as institutional credibility on the execution side.

## Why they'd buy
BLU is the textbook "ambition outrunning execution capability" case. The cap table demands delivery — IFM, KKR, Korean Gas, and Queensland Stanwell don't write checks for press releases. The April 2026 $380M raise puts a 12-24 month clock on demonstrating real operational progress.

**Tier: Watch / B-tier.** Real institutional scale-up problem with board-level decision makers. Worth a thoughtful first touch via the Chairman track if Phillips doesn't bite.
